    Research view

    Venice cleared 3.5M users and 1.3T monthly tokens by August 2026, turned profitable in Q1, and announced a $100M annualized run rate on August 17. Every Pro, Pro+ and Max subscription burns $2 to $10 of VVV directly, emissions were cut 86% to 2M a year on October 1, and 68% of the float is staked for API capacity. That is a real flywheel, and it is why VVV is up 1,335% on the year while the rest of the AI-crypto sector is still digging out. The two facts that cap size: the top 100 wallets hold over 97% of supply, and a token audit flags an uncapped owner mint with no timelock. Constructive, sized to survive both being true at once.

    Platform Overview

    Venice AI, launched in May 2024 by ShapeShift founder Erik Voorhees, with president and CTO Jesse Proudman (the project grew out of the pair's earlier Morphic and Ninji AI ventures), is a privacy-first alternative to ChatGPT. It serves open-source and proprietary models for text, image, video, code, and agentic workflows through one web app and API, with no storage of user prompts or conversations on centralized servers. Its flagship in-house model, Venice Uncensored (a 24B Dolphin Mistral collaboration), plus derivatives like Gemma 4 Uncensored, offer near-zero refusal behavior, making Venice the leading "uncensored" consumer AI brand.

    Tokenomics

    VVV launched on Base in January 2025 with a 100M supply. Since then 33.89M VVV (41.78% of original supply) has been burned, including all unclaimed airdrop tokens in March 2025. Emissions have been cut in a staircase from 14M per year to 2M as of October 1, 2026 (down 86%), with 100% of new tokens routed to stakers. Since December 2025, subscription revenue funds programmatic buy-and-burn: each new Pro, Pro+, and Max subscription triggers burns of $2, $5, and $10 respectively. Staking VVV (about 6% yield) grants a proportional daily share of API inference capacity; 33.21M of the 48.57M circulating supply is staked, and stakers can lock VVV to mint DIEM, each worth $1 of daily API credit in perpetuity (DIEM trades near $2,000).

    Usage and Business Metrics

    Venice passed 3 million users in April 2026 and 3.5 million by August, processing 1.3 trillion tokens monthly across 1.7 million-plus daily API calls. It turned profitable in Q1 2026 and announced a $100 million annualized revenue run rate on August 17, 2026.

    Recent Developments

    • Jul 1, 2026: $65M Series A at a $1B valuation led by Dragonfly, with Coinbase Ventures, North Island Ventures, Archetype, Morgan Creek, and Liquid2. VVV rose 12.8% on the news.
    • Aug-Sep 2026: Grayscale research (published Oct 2) flagged AI-crypto's 54% September gain versus 24% for the broad market, with VVV up 70%.
    • Sep 21, 2026: all-time high of $34.53.
    • Oct 1, 2026: annual emissions cut to 2M VVV.
    • Q4 2026: Venice V2 ("open platform for unrestricted intelligence") planned, with deeper VVV integration and video generation.

    Market State

    VVV trades around $27.5-29.8 (sources differ intraday, October 5), roughly 15-20% below its September ATH, with a market cap near $1.4B, 24-hour volume of $24-37M, and listings on 21 exchanges including Coinbase and Kraken. It is up sharply from a 2026 average of about $11.45 and a 2025 low near $0.92.

    Bull Case

    Real, growing revenue funding burns; profitability; 68% of circulating supply staked, tightening float; supply down 41.78% with emissions cut 86%; institutional validation from Grayscale, Dragonfly, and Coinbase Ventures; V2 and video could expand utility demand; strong AI-agent narrative fit on Base.

    Bear Case and Risks

    Top 100 wallets control over 97% of supply. An audit flags an uncapped owner mint() function with no timelock. Burns are small relative to the 2M emission schedule unless revenue compounds. Competition is intense: subsidized centralized labs, Bittensor, NEAR, and Akash, while DeepSeek-style cost collapse compresses inference margins. The September rally was sector-driven and prone to sharp corrections; FDV near $2.1B implies dilution overhang.

    12-Month Outlook

    Structurally constructive but volatile. If V2 lands and revenue keeps compounding, burns plus staking demand can absorb the now-minimal emissions, supporting a retest of $34.53 and higher. If sector momentum fades or growth stalls, concentration and thin liquidity argue for retracements toward $21-26. Watch: burn pace versus emissions, V2 adoption, and staking rate.
